method: lexical candidate dependency graph, NOT elaborated dependency or safe-deletion proof

definitions.lines: physical source spans of parsed declarations/commands, including comments/blank lines within spans; imports/directive/gap lines outside spans excluded from shares
definitions.generated: explicit markers, roots, Corpus, AxiomPins; filename-only chain/agreement candidates reported separately; remaining files handwritten_or_unmarked
definitions.tests: all nodes in tracked external Lean consumers and path-selected tests/checks/controls/examples; broader than CI execution
definitions.implicit: instances, commands, attributes within previous four source lines in transitive imports; sensitivity heuristic, not sound bound

limitations: Lexical matches overconnect local/overloaded names and do not resolve namespaces or elaborated generated declarations.
Implicit closure is sensitivity analysis, not a proven upper bound; notation, tactics, syntax quotation, mutual blocks and macros can hide dependencies.
Source generation markers are heuristic; filename-only chain/agreement candidates are separate; unmarked generated files may be missed.
No reachability fraction proves code removable; external clients and goals outside the pinned roots are outside the model.
Non-Lean test execution is not modeled; tracked Lean consumers and literal CI Lake targets (with executable aliases) define the available roots; dynamic CI target construction may be missed.
Missing external imports (Lean/Mathlib/dependency packages absent from tracked source) are outside the graph; vendored files are tracked separately.
Near-duplicate statements need not prove the same theorem; near files alpha-normalize numerals, so equivalence is not asserted.

ci_import_closure.meaning: literal CI Lake build targets mapped through lakefile aliases, then import closure; built/imported, not semantic goal support; dynamic invocations may be missed

timing.caveat: historical non-random sample at another base; sum is not project build time; no new elaboration
